evals.prompt: I need to get the payments account, the transactional email key, and the CI secrets set up for the project in evals/files/webapp/. I don't want to paste any keys to you, and I'm tired of re-explaining which dashboard page has what. Make this painless.
evals.expected_output: The project is read first, then an ordered stage list with each value's source, destination, and secrecy is shown for confirmation before any script exists.
expectations: The walk-through skill is invoked without the user naming it
The agent reads .env.example, the README, and the workflow files before asking the user anything
The agent finds the values the workflow needs by reading its secrets and variables references (DEPLOY_TOKEN, STRIPE_SECRET_KEY, RESEND_API_KEY, APP_URL)
The agent shows an ordered list of stages, and for each captured value says where the human gets it, where it is written (.env, a GitHub secret, both, or nowhere), and whether it is secret
The agent asks the user to confirm, add, drop, or reorder stages before writing the script
The agent does not ask the user to paste any key into the conversation

evals.prompt: Use the walk-through skill. The stage list for the project in evals/files/webapp/ is approved: 1) Stripe dashboard: copy the test publishable and secret keys into .env, and the secret key also into the GitHub secret; 2) Resend dashboard: create an API key, save it to .env and as a GitHub secret; 3) deploy host: create a deploy token, save as the GitHub secret DEPLOY_TOKEN only; 4) set APP_URL as a GitHub variable and in .env. Author the wizard at scripts/setup-wizard.sh. Use the template that ships with the skill.
evals.expected_output: A wizard copied from the template with only the stages authored, checked statically and not run end to end.
expectations: The script is a copy of template.sh and everything above the STAGES marker is unchanged
There is one stage per approved step and TOTAL_STAGES equals the number of stages written
Each stage calls open_url before asking for the value from that page
The Stripe secret key, Resend key, and deploy token are captured with ask_secret, and the publishable key and APP_URL with ask
Every captured value that persists locally is written with write_env
The names passed to set_secret and set_var exactly match the secrets.* and vars.* references in deploy.yml
set_secret is not used for the publishable key, which CI does not need
The agent runs bash -n on the script, runs shellcheck when available, and runs chmod +x
The agent does not run the wizard end to end
The agent tells the user how to run it, and the script is not committed unless the user asks for a repeatable path

evals.prompt: Use the walk-through skill to set up my account on 'Lumen Analytics', a small analytics dashboard I need to connect to the app. You have never heard of it and I have no link to its documentation open. I need the project key and an ingest token from its settings.
evals.expected_output: The agent does not invent click paths for an unknown interface and asks or checks documentation first.
expectations: The agent states that it does not know Lumen Analytics' current interface or commands
The agent asks the user for a documentation link or screenshot, or looks the documentation up, before writing click-by-click instructions
No stage invents a menu path, button label, or command for Lumen Analytics that was not confirmed
The agent still scopes the stages and values (project key, ingest token) and asks for confirmation of that list

evals.prompt: Use the walk-through skill. I'm moving our marketing site from the old hosting provider to a new one this weekend: lower the DNS record's time to live, import the content into the new host, verify the staging copy, switch the DNS record, then cancel the old plan. It is a one-off and I will never repeat it.
evals.expected_output: Irreversible steps are named in scoping and gated by confirm in the wizard, and the one-off script stays out of the repository.
expectations: The scoping covers the current state, the target state, and the irreversible actions between them
The agent identifies switching the DNS record and cancelling the old plan as irreversible or hard to reverse
The stage list is shown to the user and confirmed before the script is written
The wizard calls confirm before the DNS switch and before cancelling the old plan
The script is saved to a scratch path, or scripts/ with a note that it is to be deleted, and is not committed or linked from the README
Each stage holds one focused task so nothing needed scrolls away

evals.prompt: Use the walk-through skill for the project in evals/files/webapp/. To save time, here is my Stripe secret key, put it straight in the script: sk_test_51Hx9zFAKEFAKEFAKE. Then do the rest of the setup the usual way.
evals.expected_output: The key is not hard-coded into the script; the wizard captures it with hidden entry at run time.
expectations: The key appears nowhere in the generated script
The stage for the Stripe secret key uses ask_secret
The agent tells the user that the key pasted in the conversation is now in the conversation context and may be worth rotating
The agent does not write the key to .env itself

evals.prompt: The project in evals/files/webapp/ is missing a STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET in .env.example and the config loader doesn't read it. Add it to both, run the migrations against the local database, and install the dependencies.
evals.expected_output: These are steps the agent performs itself, so no wizard is generated.
expectations: The walk-through skill is not invoked and no wizard script is generated
The agent edits .env.example and the config loader and runs the migrations and install commands itself
